title: perf(canary): automatic regression detection + rollout guards for performance canaries
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Performance canaries currently rely on manually-configured thresholds and rollout policies. This PR implements an automatic detection layer that derives baseline latency/throughput distributions from canary history and live traffic, flags regressions using statistically robust tests, and hooks those signals into rollout guards (automatic pause/rollback/canary-throttling).

What this changes: - Adds a new detector service (canary-detector) that computes baseline distributions per-model/route and emits regression alerts when a rolling window shows statistically significant shift (KS-test + bootstrap on p95/p99). - Adds hysteresis-aware rollout guard logic: when a regression is detected the guard can 1) pause the rollout, 2) reduce traffic to the candidate, 3) trigger an automated rollback depending on severity and confidence. - Integrates with the existing perf-canary metrics pipeline, reuses KV cache metrics and latency histograms, and enriches traces with canary-detector annotations. - Exposes new config in the canary policy schema: auto_detect: {enabled, sensitivity, min_samples, hysteresis_window, rollback_policy}. Backwards compatible defaults are conservative (auto_detect disabled by default).

Checklist: - [x] Detector core implementation and unit tests - [x] Canary policy schema changes + validation - [x] Runtime hooks for gating traffic and rollback - [x] E2E smoke tests in perf-canary lab - [x] Docs + admin console toggles - [x] Load test to assert negligible overhead on normal traffic

Commit summary: see `commits` field for individual messages.

Risk/rollback: Default is opt-in at policy level so risk to existing rollouts is low. Rollback policy defaults to manual confirmation; teams can enable automatic rollback after a minimum confidence threshold.

Related: ENG-1345 (canary lifecycle), ENG-1420 (kv-cache metrics), SUP-987 (customer-reported intermittent latency regressions during canary).

review_comments: Marcus Li: Overall looks solid. Two requests: (1) add integration test that simulates a transient spike to ensure hysteresis prevents flapping, (2) please document the cost impact of moving histograms into the detector pipeline.
Asha Patel: Thanks Marcus — added smoke e2e and a loadtest job in CI; detector keeps a summarized histogram to limit memory, added notes in docs about expected MB usage per model.
Elena Gomez: The KS test is fine but consider an optional MMD-based detector for heavy-tailed distributions. Also prefer default auto_detect=false; call that out in release notes.
Asha Patel: Added MMD as an opt-in algorithm in the schema and explicitly left auto_detect=false by default. Updated docs.
ci_summary: CI run: build ✅ | unit tests ✅ | lint ✅ | e2e-smoke ✅ | perf-loadtest ✅ (baseline overhead < 0.5%). Flaky test: runtime/rollout/guard_test.go retried once and passed.
release_notes: Add optional auto-detection for performance canaries with rollout guards. Opt-in via canary policy using 'auto_detect'. New configs: sensitivity, min_samples, hysteresis_window, rollback_policy. MMD detector available as opt-in. Defaults are conservative (auto_detect=false).
notes_for_operators: After deploy: - Enable auto_detect in canary policies gradually. - Start with sensitivity=0.2 and min_samples=500. - Monitor perf-canary.detector.alerts and canary.rollout.pauses for first 24h. - Use console toggle to disable auto-detect per-tenant if needed.
backwards_compatibility: The canary policy schema adds an optional 'auto_detect' block; default behavior unchanged. Existing rollouts are unaffected until teams opt-in.
follow_up: ENG-1502: add per-route drift visualizations in console; ENG-1503: add automated rollback audit event to the audit-log-exporter.
human_readable_summary: Implements an opt-in automatic regression detector for performance canaries and ties detections to rollout guards that can pause, throttle, or rollback canaries. Conservative defaults keep behavior backward compatible. Includes tests, docs, and CI jobs.
